question: Can per-example evolutionary search over intermediate activation tensors produce diverse label-fitting targets that a separate network can regress to, thereby offering a useful alternative path to models normally obtained by end-to-end classification gradients?

key_findings.claim: The method searches label-conditioned activations for each training image independently; it does not directly search a coherent representation function or a model shared across the dataset.
key_findings.evidence: At every layer, top-k selection and fitness evaluation are independent per image, and fitness is negative cross-entropy against that image's true label. The best activation sequence for each example is cached, after which a separate parameterized network learns a mapping to those targets.

key_findings.claim: The assertion that representation space is smaller and therefore more tractable than parameter space is not established for the dataset-level problem.
key_findings.evidence: A single block-0 target contains 256 x 15 x 15 = 57,600 values per example, and the method searches and caches targets at four levels for every training item. Although one per-example tensor can be smaller than all model parameters, the joint target collection scales with dataset size and can greatly exceed the parameter count; the paper reports neither total target dimensionality nor storage and search FLOPs.

anchors.section: Appendix A.2, population and generation schedule

key_findings.claim: The evolutionary stage is a heavily engineered, label-supervised target generator rather than a general search for a simplicity-biased model.
key_findings.evidence: Candidates are averaged, perturbed with per-channel Gaussian noise, spatially blurred, standardized, and selected by true-label cross-entropy. The introductory Solomonoff-style generalization prior is never instantiated: no simplicity objective, held-out fitness, or model-level selection enters evolution.

anchors.section: Appendix A.4, crossover, mutation, smoothing, and normalization

key_findings.claim: The convolutional body avoids direct cross-entropy gradients, but it still uses ordinary backpropagation on strongly label-conditioned regression targets.
key_findings.evidence: Every block is optimized with MSE to cached searched activations, and the classification head receives KL gradients from searched logits. Stop-gradient prevents that KL term from reaching the body; it does not remove backward differentiation of the layerwise MSE losses.

key_findings.claim: Without augmentation, searched-target learning nearly matches but does not exceed the selected SGD baseline on any reported dataset.
key_findings.evidence: Across three runs, SGD versus search-based test accuracy is 99.1±0.1 versus 99.0±0.1 on MNIST, 89.1±0.3 versus 88.3±0.3 on CIFAR-10, and 62.3±0.5 versus 61.6±0.2 on CIFAR-100.

key_findings.claim: Under augmentation, early-layer target regression is actively harmful, and even the best skip-block variant remains below SGD.
key_findings.evidence: On CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, SGD reaches 93.0±0.2/71.8±0.4, all-layer target supervision reaches 90.6±0.3/66.5±0.3, and omitting direct block-0 supervision improves this to 92.0±0.1/69.2±0.3. The paper reuses one cached target across augmented variants of an image, so low-level targets need not transform consistently with crops and flips.

anchors.section: Sections 4.2-4.3, supervision variants and cached augmentation

key_findings.claim: The reported fitness-compute trend is real for best-of-population training loss, but it does not by itself establish more efficient learning.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 2 averages the best candidate's cross-entropy on 1,000 CIFAR-100 training points as population size or generations increase. Best-of-more-samples performance is expected to improve mechanically, and no equal-FLOP optimizer, wall-clock, or sample-efficiency baseline is shown.

key_findings.claim: The diversity-scaling experiment mainly shows that the effective number of solutions rises as more independent solutions are included in the estimator.
key_findings.evidence: Each independent run contributes its top activation only if correct-class probability exceeds 0.5, and Figure 3 plots N_eff against the number of aggregated runs. This can demonstrate non-identical accepted samples, but it does not isolate whether larger populations or more generations make each run more diverse, and comparisons across blocks are confounded by activation dimension.

anchors.section: Section 3.2, Diversity scaling and collision entropy

key_findings.claim: Cosine distance from SGD activations does not establish discovery of functionally distinct model solutions.
key_findings.evidence: The paper reports SGD-to-target cosine distance near one and differing collision-entropy trajectories, but hidden representations admit neuron permutations, rotations, rescalings, and other function-preserving reparameterizations. No alignment method, function-space disagreement, ensemble gain, error complementarity, or interpolation barrier is measured.

key_findings.claim: The complete default search is computationally substantial and its end-to-end cost is left unaudited.
key_findings.evidence: The default population is 240 per image, retaining 20 parents and generating 220 children per generation, with schedules of 300, 100, 100, and 10 generations across the four search levels. Every mutated candidate is forwarded through downstream blocks, then all per-example targets are cached before 90 epochs of regression training; no GPU-hours, FLOPs, peak memory, cache size, or energy comparison to SGD is reported.

key_findings.claim: The work is a one-shot proof of concept, not yet the proposed amortized search-learning cycle.
key_findings.evidence: Search uses an untrained initialized network once; cached targets never change as the learner improves. The conclusion explicitly identifies iterative feedback, stronger performance, and evidence that representation diversity yields model diversity as future work.

method.core_idea: First evolve a separate label-fitting activation sequence for each training example, layer by layer, and then train a deeper convolutional model with backpropagation to regress to those fixed activation targets while isolating its body from direct classification-loss gradients.
method.mechanism: A fixed initialized CNN produces populations of candidate block activations. For each image, evolution retains its top-k candidates under true-label cross-entropy, averages parent pairs, adds channel-wise Gaussian mutations, smooths convolutional noise, standardizes candidates, and forwards them through all remaining blocks. Earlier evolved layers are fixed while later layers are searched. The best activation and logit sequence is cached per training example. A separate higher-capacity network minimizes per-layer MSE; its head also matches searched logits with KL divergence, with stop-gradient at the body-head boundary. Search compute is varied through population size and generations, and learned models are compared to selected-depth SGD baselines.
assumptions: Per-example label-fitting activations can be combined into a learnable shared function rather than an inconsistent lookup table.
Intermediate targets discovered under an untrained shallower search network remain appropriate for a deeper learning network.
Gaussian mutation, spatial blur, and per-sample standardization encode a useful prior over learnable representations.
Sequentially freezing early targets does not block globally better joint activation configurations.
True-label cross-entropy fitness produces targets with inductive bias beyond simply encoding the label.
Cached targets remain semantically valid after random crops and horizontal flips.
Cosine and collision-entropy differences correspond to meaningful functional diversity rather than coordinate symmetries or dimensionality.
The compute and storage cost of per-example evolution can scale to datasets and architectures of practical interest.
A generalization prior will emerge from the search operators or subsequent regression despite not appearing explicitly in the fitness.

techniques.role: Maintain a distinct population of intermediate tensors for each labeled example.
Optimize a block output, freeze its best candidate, and continue through later blocks.
Retain top parents, average pairs, and generate high-strength exploration plus lower-strength refinement children.
Blur convolutional perturbations to reduce high-frequency targets that the learner cannot fit.
Normalize evolved convolutional activations to stabilize evolutionary convergence.
Train the model body by MSE to a fixed activation sequence computed before learning.
Match searched logits with KL only in the head, preventing classification gradients from entering the body.
Summarize cosine-Gram similarity as an effective number of orthogonal activation solutions.

evaluations.setting: CIFAR-100 training examples, separately evolving each of three convolutional block outputs while varying population size or generation count.
evaluations.metric: Mean best-candidate cross-entropy across 1,000 training points.
evaluations.result: Training fitness improves with both compute knobs and later blocks are easier to optimize.
evaluations.baseline: Smaller populations or fewer generations only; no equal-FLOP SGD, random-target, or direct-logit-search baseline.

evaluations.setting: Independent CIFAR-100 evolutionary runs at each block, retaining candidates with correct-class probability above 0.5.
evaluations.metric: Effective solution count derived from collision entropy of the cosine Gram matrix.
evaluations.result: N_eff rises as more independent accepted candidates are aggregated, with the largest values at the highest-dimensional early block.
evaluations.baseline: No dimension-matched random vectors, shuffled candidates, parameter-space search, or fixed-run-count comparison across compute settings.

evaluations.setting: MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 without augmentation, using three independent runs.
evaluations.result: Search-based learning reaches 99.0±0.1, 88.3±0.3, and 61.6±0.2, respectively, versus SGD's 99.1±0.1, 89.1±0.3, and 62.3±0.5.
evaluations.baseline: Best-performing SGD architecture among two, four, and six convolutional layers per block; no total-compute matching.

evaluations.setting: CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 with random crops and flips, reusing one cached target sequence per original image.
evaluations.metric: Mean test accuracy ± standard deviation across three runs.
evaluations.result: Skipping direct block-0 supervision reaches 92.0±0.1 and 69.2±0.3; all-layer supervision reaches 90.6±0.3 and 66.5±0.3; SGD reaches 93.0±0.2 and 71.8±0.4.
evaluations.baseline: Selected SGD and two target-supervision variants; no equivariant target transformation or online re-search.

evaluations.setting: CIFAR-100 learners trained on caches produced with different search populations and generation counts.
evaluations.result: Accuracy generally rises with either search-compute knob and then saturates.
evaluations.baseline: Lower search budgets; axes do not establish matched total FLOPs or statistical uncertainty.

evaluations.setting: CIFAR-100 validation activations over training for searched-target and SGD models.
evaluations.metric: Cosine distance to cached targets and within/between-class collision entropy.
evaluations.result: The target-trained model approaches its cached activations, while SGD remains near cosine distance one and follows different entropy trajectories.
evaluations.baseline: Raw SGD coordinates without permutation, rotation, CKA, function-space, ensemble, or mode-connectivity alignment.

limitations: The search is per-example and label-conditioned, so it never evaluates a shared model's generalization during evolution.
Representation-space tractability is asserted from local tensor size rather than demonstrated for the full dataset-level target collection.
No wall-clock, FLOP, peak-memory, cache-storage, or energy accounting accompanies a population of 240 over 510 scheduled generations per example.
Performance remains below selected SGD on every benchmark, and only MNIST/CIFAR-scale convolutional models are evaluated.
The all-layer method degrades substantially under augmentation; skipping the earliest target only partially closes the gap.
One cached target is reused for all augmented views without a target-equivariance mechanism.
Only three learning runs are reported, and search-run uncertainty is not propagated into final accuracy.
The diversity metric is coordinate- and dimension-sensitive and is not connected to predictive disagreement or ensemble benefit.
Fitness scaling uses best-of-more-search without a compute-matched optimization baseline.
Search and learning occur once rather than in the motivating iterative amortization loop.
The proposed Solomonoff-like generalization prior is conceptual and absent from the implemented objective.
Results depend on manual choices of population, top-k, mutation strengths, exploration boosts, blur passes, layer schedule, loss weights, and extra learner depth.
failure_modes: Evolution can create per-example targets that encode labels but are mutually inconsistent with any smooth shared input-to-representation function.
Earlier layer targets can overfit pixel coordinates and conflict with crops, flips, or other invariances.
Greedy freezing can lock in an early activation that makes later layers fit the label but is globally poor for learnability.
High-dimensional random activations can appear diverse under cosine geometry even when they provide no useful functional alternatives.
Searching logits can dominate fitness while intermediate mutations contribute little beyond noisy target regularization.
Caching four high-dimensional tensors per sample can become prohibitive before model parameter size becomes the bottleneck.
A learner with insufficient capacity can fail to regress the large activation jumps; increasing depth can hide rather than solve target inconsistency.
An untrained network's downstream mapping may give an arbitrary and architecture-specific fitness landscape.
The true-label fitness can leak annotation noise directly into expensive per-example target search.
A fixed cache cannot adapt when the learner's representation basis changes or when new data arrive.
reusable_insights: Treat intermediate activations as explicit optimization variables, but validate their joint realizability by a shared function before scaling search.
Separate target discovery from target amortization so each stage can be evaluated independently.
Spatial smoothing can serve as a learnability prior for searched feature maps, provided it is ablated against cheaper fixed smoothing targets.
When augmentation changes the input geometry, transform or regenerate low-level targets equivariantly.
Measure diversity in both aligned representation space and function space; only the latter establishes distinct useful predictors.
Compare best-of-N search to equal-compute random search and gradient-based activation optimization to isolate evolutionary value.
Iterative search-learning cycles should refresh targets selectively where learner residuals reveal inconsistency.
Dataset-level dimensionality, cache bytes, and forward evaluations are the relevant scaling quantities for per-example latent search.
open_questions: Does evolutionary activation search outperform direct gradient optimization of the same tensors under equal forward/backward FLOPs?
How much of the result survives if intermediate evolution is removed and only searched or smoothed logits are distilled?
Can a conditional target generator amortize the cache and produce targets for unseen examples before seeing their labels?
Do separately evolved targets satisfy measurable Lipschitz, margin, or local-consistency conditions required for shared learnability?
Can an explicit simplicity, invariance, or held-out fitness term produce actual generalization gains beyond SGD?
What happens when all layer activations are evolved jointly instead of greedily frozen?
Does target diversity yield predictive disagreement, complementary errors, robust ensembles, or different OOD behavior after alignment?
What are end-to-end GPU-hours, FLOPs, cache bytes, and carbon cost relative to SGD at matched accuracy?
Can augmentations act inside search so every view receives an equivariant or invariant target?
Does a closed search-learn-refresh loop improve targets, or collapse diversity toward the current learner?

competitive_landscape.title: Towards Scaling Difference Target Propagation by Learning Backprop Targets
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct layerwise-target-learning predecessor at larger vision scale.
competitive_landscape.difference: Difference target propagation learns feedback pathways with an explicit Gauss-Newton connection and reports CIFAR-10 plus ImageNet-32 results; this paper obtains fixed per-example targets through evolutionary activation search and offers no corresponding update theory.

competitive_landscape.title: The Forward-Forward Algorithm: Some Preliminary Investigations
competitive_landscape.relationship: Alternative nonstandard credit-assignment framework using local layer objectives.
competitive_landscape.difference: Forward-Forward trains layers from positive and negative passes without stored searched tensors, whereas this method still backpropagates MSE to a large offline cache of label-conditioned activations.

competitive_landscape.title: Evolution Strategies as a Scalable Alternative to Reinforcement Learning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Foundational large-scale black-box parameter optimization comparator.
competitive_landscape.difference: Evolution Strategies searches a distribution over shared policy parameters and scales through common-random-number parallelism; this work searches separate activations for each labeled example, then amortizes them with supervised regression.

competitive_landscape.title: Deep Neuroevolution: Genetic Algorithms Are a Competitive Alternative for Training Deep Neural Networks for Reinforcement Learning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Counterexample to the paper's broad claim that parameter-space evolutionary search is intractable.
competitive_landscape.difference: Deep GA evolves shared networks with more than four million parameters and novelty search on RL tasks. It is expensive but demonstrates tractability through compact perturbation encodings and parallelism; activation search instead pays per-example population and cache costs.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Network Diffusion
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct generative alternative for exploring trained neural-network solutions.
competitive_landscape.difference: It learns a latent diffusion distribution over high-performing parameter subsets and samples complete usable weights; this paper avoids parameter generation by searching per-example activations but must subsequently train a network to realize them.

competitive_landscape.title: Searching Latent Program Spaces
competitive_landscape.relationship: Current learned-latent-search approach with explicit unseen-task adaptation.
competitive_landscape.difference: LPN learns a compact latent program distribution and searches it at test time on ARC-style tasks, directly testing adaptation beyond the training distribution. This work searches observed training examples only and freezes its cache before learning.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning to Synthesize Programs as Interpretable and Generalizable Policies
competitive_landscape.difference: LEAPS first learns a continuous program embedding and then searches it for reward-maximizing interpretable policies, evaluating task generalization. The reviewed paper directly mutates raw hidden activations without learning a search-space prior or testing target search on unseen tasks.
competitive_landscape.source_version: NeurIPS 2021, Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 34

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors frame the work as a first step toward overcoming gradient descent's exploratory limits by moving explicit evolutionary search into a tractable intermediate-representation space and using gradient learning only to realize the searched solutions.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The exact combination of per-image, layer-sequential activation evolution, cached multi-level targets, body-isolated MSE regression, and compute/diversity plots is distinctive. However, target propagation already trains toward layerwise targets, Forward-Forward supplies local alternatives, parameter-space ES/GA demonstrate scalable evolutionary training, neural-network diffusion generates parameter solutions, and latent-program methods already decouple representation learning from downstream search with explicit generalization tests.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Novel as a concrete exploratory prototype for evolving raw intermediate tensors and amortizing them into a classifier, but not yet evidence that this is a more tractable, diverse, or generalizing training paradigm. The method searches labels independently rather than models, remains uniformly below SGD, lacks end-to-end compute accounting, and measures representation diversity without functional validation. Its most valuable contribution is an experimental scaffold for testing searched targets, not a demonstrated replacement for gradient descent or a realized generalization prior.

reviewer_notes: Sole-writer first-pass review of all 14 pages of the exact indexed PDF, including the conceptual argument, full evolutionary operators, compute/diversity definitions, both accuracy tables, representation analyses, limitations, and hyperparameters. All reported accuracy values and schedules were checked against Tables 1-2 and Appendix A. Competing work was independently checked on primary arXiv, PMLR, and NeurIPS proceedings records on 2026-08-23, including post-submission Latent Program Network revisions. Confidence is high for the protocol and construct-validity audit; it is slightly lower for compute magnitude because the paper omits runtime, hardware, cache size, and implementation code measurements, so no unreported cost is numerically imputed.
